svg.aria-label: How to write ந, ன, ற: 3 letters, ந, ன, ற, one after another
svg.title: Writing ந, ன, ற
svg.desc: 3 letters written one after another: ந, ன, ற (tamil). Each letter has its own group of frames; frame N of a group shows movements 1 to N of that letter, the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansTamil-Static.ttf. Each letter is drawn at its own scale from its own cited stroke order, so the strip does not show how large the letters are next to each other, how far apart they sit, or any join between them. Stroke order: ந: Sankaran Radhakrishnan, Tamil Script Learners Manual, Appendix I: Hand-movements, Frame 5, ந (University of Texas at Austin), p. 193 <https://sites.la.utexas.edu/tamilscript/files/2009/08/hw_lettersinstructions.pdf>; ன: Sankaran Radhakrishnan, Tamil Script Learners Manual, Appendix I: Hand-movements, Frame 13, ன (Univ. of Texas at Austin), p. 195 <https://sites.la.utexas.edu/tamilscript/files/2009/08/hw_lettersinstructions.pdf>; ற: Sankaran Radhakrishnan, Tamil Script Learners Manual, Appendix I: Hand-movements, Frame 10, ற (Univ. of Texas at Austin), p. 194 <https://sites.la.utexas.edu/tamilscript/files/2009/08/hw_lettersinstructions.pdf>. Source notes on variation: ந: Module 5 identifies ந as the voiced dental nasal and notes that its extended final curve may be omitted. Appendix I Frame 5 numbers six hand-movements. Native writers draw them as one continuous stroke, and this ductus follows the six movements in order without lifting: the pen climbs back up the middle upright to where the right bowl leaves it. In HP Labs India's online Tamil handwriting data (the LipiTk 4.0 Tamil isolated-character recognizer, trained on hpl-tamil-iso-char), 85% of the 224 stored prototypes of ந are a single pen-down stroke. Tamil handwriting varies by school; this is one attested order fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Tamil outline. ன: Tamil handwriting is taught with school-to-school variation; there is no single national stroke-order standard. Appendix I Frame 13 numbers six hand-movements for ன. Native writers draw them as one continuous stroke, and this ductus follows the six movements in order without lifting: the top bar runs out to the right edge, so the pen comes back along it to the right upright and draws the upright down. In HP Labs India's online Tamil handwriting data (the LipiTk 4.0 Tamil isolated-character recognizer, trained on hpl-tamil-iso-char), 94% of the 335 stored prototypes of ன are a single pen-down stroke. ற: Tamil handwriting is taught with school-to-school variation; there is no single national stroke-order standard. Appendix I Frame 10 numbers five hand-movements, with movement 3 on the middle upright beside movement 2. Native writers draw them as one continuous stroke, and this ductus follows the five movements in order without lifting. The bundled Noto Sans Tamil outline prints a single shared middle upright, so movement 3 climbs back up it to start the second arch. In HP Labs India's online Tamil handwriting data (the LipiTk 4.0 Tamil isolated-character recognizer, trained on hpl-tamil-iso-char), 99% of the 378 stored prototypes of ற are a single pen-down stroke.
svg.text: How it is written — 3 letters, one after another
Letter 1 of 3 — one unbroken stroke · 6 movements
Letter 2 of 3 — one unbroken stroke · 6 movements
Letter 3 of 3 — one unbroken stroke · 5 movements
Letter 1: stroke order after Sankaran Radhakrishnan, Tamil Script Learners Manual, Appendix I: Hand-movements, Frame 5, ந (University of Texas at Austin), p. 193
Letter 2: stroke order after Sankaran Radhakrishnan, Tamil Script Learners Manual, Appendix I: Hand-movements, Frame 13, ன (Univ. of Texas at Austin), p. 195
Letter 3: stroke order after Sankaran Radhakrishnan, Tamil Script Learners Manual, Appendix I: Hand-movements, Frame 10, ற (Univ. of Texas at Austin), p. 194
This order is attested, not standardised; the source records where it varies.
